title: Owner-auth policy
description: The owner-auth policy (F1c): which signals mark a worker environment (bin/worker_env.py), which owner-authenticator providers exist and which proofs each action needs (bin/owner_auth.py). Owner-only and identity-critical: only the owner path writes it.

providers.description: The owner-authenticator providers (F1c D2). The kind is code (bin/owner_auth.py); which ones exist and what each action class needs is this data. A new provider of a known kind (a command, say) is a new row: no code change. owner_auth.py check also requires each id once and the params of its kind: local-key, typed-phrase, device-phrase none; device-signature timeout_s (of its openssl check); channel-identity channel_kind and owner_config_key; command argv and timeout_s.

kind.description: local-key: an HMAC with the owner key file (index owner_key) on the host. channel-identity: the answer's user id equals the owner config value named by owner_config_key, on the message the caller delivered. command: argv runs with the request as JSON on stdin; exit 0 = valid, within timeout_s. typed-phrase: the rendered phrase typed on the host terminal. device-phrase: the device-signed payload's phrase equals the rendered phrase (stands only beside a device-signature provider). device-signature: a paired device of the devices row (not revoked) signed {digest, nonce, expires_at, device_id[, phrase]} with its Ed25519 key; each accepted one is a remote owner change (remote: one alert, rate limited).

owner_config_key.description: The name (never the value) of the owner config key that holds the owner's user id on that channel.

argv.description: The command; its first item is an absolute path.

actions.description: Action class -> alternatives; an alternative is a list of provider ids that must all pass, and one passing alternative is enough. owner_write: an owner data change; channel_answer: an approval answered on a channel; identity_critical: used instead of owner_write when the change touches an identity-critical target. owner_auth.py check requires every id to be a provider.

template.description: The confirmation phrase; {what} becomes the action's target.

proof_ttl_s.description: How long a proof made on the host stays valid (prove's default and maximum); a proof that expires later than this from now is refused.

worker_signals.description: Any one signal makes this process a worker environment: every owner command refuses, the trusted event writer included (STL-CFG-312); agents write only to the untrusted stream through bin/event_untrusted.py (F1c B4, B7). These add to the role table's worker_markers and roles.py prove.

token_env.description: Environment variables that carry an agent token: set and not empty = a worker.

users.description: OS user names agents run as (empty until E1 adds the agent user).

sandbox_files.description: Absolute paths whose existence marks the agent sandbox.

worktree_dirs.description: Folders (relative to the stack root) whose sub-folders are run worktrees: a process whose working folder lies in one is a worker.

identity_critical.description: Identity-critical targets (F1c B3, D2): a change that touches one needs the identity_critical action class (the typed phrase) instead of owner_write. `<row id>`: any change of that index row; `<row id>:<JSON pointer>`: a change at or below that pointer, where a * segment stands for any one segment (an env row's keys are top-level members, /KEY). Settings whose registry sensitivity is identity_critical count too, without being listed here.

channel_kinds.description: Channel kind -> whether an answer on a channel of that kind may decide an approval (bin/approvals.py, F1c B2, D3). Open map: a new kind is data (a channels row of that kind plus its entry here and a channel-identity provider). A kind not listed here answers nothing (fail closed). The kind voice_host_confirmation.channel_kind (voice) answers only through that entry, whatever its value here.

voice_host_confirmation.description: The one exception to 'a voice channel answers no approval' (F1c B2, decided 2026-11-13): when enabled, the voice profile `profile` may give the quick confirmation for its own ask-first host action, a request of class action_class whose ttl is at most max_ttl_s, answered with the digest of the details shown; never any other approval. Off until the post-1.0 host operator exists. The schema keeps it strict: no other key.

channel_kind.description: The voice channel kind: a channel of this kind answers only through this entry, whatever channel_kinds says.

profile.description: The requester profile whose own asks voice may confirm.

max_ttl_s.description: The longest request ttl (seconds) voice may confirm.

action_class.description: The approval class of the host ask-first action (an approval_class of the approval-request schema).

remote.description: Owner changes from a remote device (F1c B6, D5): every accepted device-signature proof writes one alert with alert_code (a catalog code) and counts toward rate_limit; the next one past count within window_s seconds is refused STL-OWN-813. Required when a device-signature provider is listed (owner_auth.py check).

alert_code.description: The alert-catalog code of the alert each remote owner change raises.
